# Zomato is shutting down its 10-minute food delivery business
Zomato is shutting down its 10-minute food delivery business
...
The company recently communicated to restaurant partners that it would look to close down the service, said two sources privy to the development.
ETtech
Zomato is shutting down its 10-minute food delivery service Zomato Instant less than a year after it was launched as it chases profitability amid tough market conditions.
The company recently told its restaurant partners it would look to close down the service, said two sources privy to the development.
“It didn’t look like it would turn profitable.
The company was not getting the daily volume required to even pay the fixed costs.
It wasn't scaling up to that level,” a person aware of the development told ET Prime.
“The plan is to now pivot to a new product,” he said, adding that Zomato is experimenting with low-value packed meals – thalis or combo meals.
It has not been decided if Zomato will retain the 10-minutes preposition for this.
However the new offering will be launched in 7-10 days, one of the sources said.
However, Zomato said it was not shutting down Instant but rebranding the service.
"Instant is not shutting down.
We are working on a new menu with our partners and rebranding the business.
All finishing stations remain intact, and no people are impacted by this decision," the company said
